title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation, and QBR Health-Check Playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes for enterprise onboarding, technical integration, escalation handling, and recurring health checks / QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and Product Owners running production inference workloads.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers by standardizing onboarding steps.
- Ensure predictable, documented responses for production incidents and escalations.
- Provide a repeatable integration checklist for APIs, security, and observability.
- Deliver a QBR and health-check cadence that surfaces risk early and drives product and ops improvements.

Audience and Ownership:
- Primary audience: CSMs, SEs, Support, Engineering reps.
- Playbook owner: customer-success team (primary), eng-platform and eng-sre (secondary).
- Point-of-contact: CSM Team Lead (csm-leads@redwood-inference.internal).

1) Enterprise Onboarding Overview:

Intro:
Onboarding is split into two phases: Enablement (weeks 0-2) and Stabilization (weeks 3-12). The typical enterprise onboarding timeline is 4-12 weeks depending on integration complexity and compliance needs.

Checklist (Enablement):
- Kickoff meeting: attendees = CSM, SE, customer engineering lead, security contact, account exec. Agenda includes goals, success metrics, timeline, sample workloads.
- Account provisioning: create tenant, RBAC roles, initial API keys. Owner: provisioning SRE.
- Network setup: determine using Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. If Private, begin VPC peering or on-prem packaging request.
- Security review: exchange security questionnaire, confirm KMS/HSM integration requirements.
- Quickstart integration: SE runs customer through a 15-30 min sample request generating latencies and token usage.
- Instrumentation hooks: confirm customer ingestion into tracing (OpenTelemetry), logging endpoints, and metric exports (Prometheus/Grafana).

Checklist (Stabilization):
- Traffic ramp plan: agree on stepwise traffic ramp (e.g., 10qps -> 50qps -> 200qps) with staging tests at each step.
- Latency SLOs: baseline latencies captured and agreed. Typical SLOs: p95 < 350ms for short-form generation (<=512 tokens) on Dedicated; p95 < 800ms on Hosted for larger models.
- Cost guardrails: set rate limits, quotas, and cost alerts. Owner: CSM + finance contact.
- Quality evaluation: define prompt suite and automated evals for regressions; schedule weekly checks for first 30 days.
- Ramp completion sign-off: business owner and CSM sign-off to enter steady-state support.

Deliverables and Templates:
- Onboarding plan template: attach to the customer record (template id: onboarding-plan-v2).
- Integration checklist (technical): use the JSON example below as part of the SE packet.

Example integration config (JSON snippet):
{
  "api_base": "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1",
  "auth": "Bearer <API_KEY>",
  "model": "redwood-30b-instruct",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "timeout_ms": "120000"
}

2) Integration Guide (Technical Checklist):

Networking and Security:
- Hosted: confirm IP allowlist and CORS settings if required.
- Dedicated: confirm private peering config, NAT/firewall rules, and dedicated subnet sizing.
- Private: confirm air-gapped packaging schedule and HSM/KMS configuration.
- TLS: ensure TLS 1.2+; certificate rotation policy assigned.

Authentication and RBAC:
- Create scoped API keys and service accounts.
- Apply least-privilege roles: read-only telemetry, generator, admin.
- MFA required for console access for >10-user orgs.

Observability and Instrumentation:
- Integrate request tracing with OpenTelemetry: include trace_id in SDK requests.
- Expose per-route token cost metrics via Prometheus metric names: ri_tokens_total, ri_latency_ms_bucket.
- Enable structured logging for failed requests: include request_id, model, prompt_id.

Rate Limits and Quotas:
- Default soft quota: 500k tokens/day for trial; Enterprise quotas negotiated.
- Circuit breaker: automatic soft-fail to lower-capacity model variant at 90% quota.

3) Support Process and Escalation Playbook:

Support tiers:
- Tier 1: CSM + Support Engineers (business/process questions). Response SLA: 4 business hours.
- Tier 2: Platform Support (prod issues, telemetry triage). Response SLA: 2 business hours.
- Tier 3: Eng-serving-runtime / On-call SWAT (severe incidents, P1/P0). Response SLA: 30 minutes.

Incident Severity Matrix:
- P0 (Service down / major data loss): platform unavailable for >50% of customers or PII exposure. Escalate immediately to on-call eng-sre, notify execs.
- P1 (Significant degradation): major latency/throughput regression impacting SLAs for an enterprise customer. Escalate to platform on-call and engineering.
- P2 (Partial impact): single-customer errors, degraded performance under thresholds. Handled by Platform Support with CSM coordination.
- P3 (Minor): documentation/UX issues, feature requests. Handled by Support with backlog entry.

Escalation steps (numbered):
1. Triage in Support queue: gather customer tenant id, request_id, timeline, and recent logs.
2. Reproduce in staging if possible; collect p95/p99 latencies and error rates.
3. If P1/P0, open incident in PagerDuty and follow oncall runbook: include playbook runbook id = "oncall-runtime-p0".
4. Notify customer via designated channel (email + designated Slack/Teams channel).
5. Post-incident: write a 72-hour incident summary and schedule a 1-week follow-up with engineering and customer.

Contact matrix (examples):
- Support queue: support@redwood-inference.internal (monitored 24/5).
- PagerDuty: eng-platform-oncall (PD escalation policy).
- CSM escalation: csm-escalations@redwood-inference.internal.

4) Known Issues and Workarounds (selected):

Issue: Intermittent 504s on long-running streaming requests
- Symptom: streaming responses terminate with 504 after ~60s for large generation jobs.
- Root cause (common): load-balancer default idle timeout and upstream kernel stalls under specific KV-cache sizes.
- Workarounds:
  - For Hosted customers: reduce chunk size and enable chunked streaming via SDK flag streaming_chunk_ms=200.
  - For Dedicated/Private: increase LB idle timeout to 120s and upgrade runtime to kernel patch v2.4.1.
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Issue: Elevated token cost due to unexpected caching misses
- Symptom: daily token usage spikes without corresponding traffic increases.
- Root cause: prompt variation eliminated cache hits (different user metadata appended).
- Workarounds:
  - Normalize user metadata outside prompts or use prefix caching via SDK option enable_prefix_cache=true.
  - Set up token usage alerts to detect >30% day-over-day increase.
- Owner: eng-platform + CSM.

Known issues table (plain text):
| id | title | symptom | workaround | owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KI-101 | Streaming 504s | streaming abort at ~60s | adjust LB timeout / patch runtime | eng-serving-runtime |
| KI-207 | Cache misses | token spike | enable_prefix_cache, normalize prompts | eng-platform |

5) Health Checks and QBR Materials:

Health check cadence:
- Week 1-4: weekly health check calls between CSM, SE, and customer engineering. Focus areas: latency, error rates, cost, and quality regressions.
- Month 2-3: bi-weekly.
- Post-stabilization: monthly or quarterly depending on spend and risk.

Standard health-check dashboard (items to include):
- API success rate (goal > 99.9%).
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route and model.
- Token usage and cost per model per route.
- Error categories (400/401/429/500/502/504) with 7d trend.
- Quality regressions from evals (pass/fail on canonical prompt set).

QBR template (sections):
1. Executive summary: spend, latency, uptime, top wins/risks.
2. Product metrics: model usage, token cost, error trends.
3. Operational review: incidents since last QBR, action items and status.
4. Roadmap alignment: upcoming platform changes that affect customer (e.g., quantization profiles, kernel upgrades).
5. Recommendations and next steps: batching, caching, model variant suggestions to reduce cost or improve latency.

QBR deliverables (checklist):
- Dashboard export (last 90 days) as PDF.
- Action items with owners and due dates.
- Follow-up integration tasks logged in Jira with EPIC link.

6) Templates and Example Communications:

Initial onboarding email (template):
Subject: Redwood Inference Onboarding Plan and Kickoff
Body: Hi <Customer Team>,
We're excited to get you started. Attached is the onboarding plan with proposed dates for the kickoff, provisioning checklist, and a short technical questionnaire. Please reply with confirmed attendees for the kickoff.

P0 incident notification (template):
Subject: P0 Incident - Redwood Inference - <short description>
Body: We are investigating a P0 impacting inference for <tenant>. Current status: <summary>. Next update: in 15 minutes. Contact: <oncall name> via PagerDuty.

7) Reporting and Continuous Improvement:

Post-onboarding review (30/90-day):
- 30-day check: confirm SLA attainment, quality baselines, and any integration gaps.
- 90-day review: review costs vs. forecast, optimization wins, and propose Dedicated/Private if applicable.

Feedback loop to Product/Engineering:
- Create tagged Jira tickets for recurring integration pain points (label: customer-onboarding).
- Quarterly synapse meeting between CS leads and eng-platform to prioritize systemic improvements.
